title: Eurostat euro-area HICP, complete September 2026 data — the component detail behind the 3.8% flash
source: EST: Eurostat's own September flash release (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-02102026-ap, published 2026-10-02, fetched direct 2026-10-13) states full September data is 'scheduled for October 16, 2026'; the ECB statistical release calendar (press/calendars/statscal/ges/html/sthicp.en.html, fetched direct 2026-10-13) lists '16/10/2026 12:00 — Euro area seasonally adjusted HICP … September 2026'. Two primaries agree; STAYS ESTIMATE per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the calendar carries no confirmed source prefix for a non-US statistical agency (the same convention the two sibling Eurostat entries closed out under). Checked 2026-10-13
notes: DISCOVERED during the ecb-decision-2026-10-29 D-16 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-10-13). It earns a row because it is the scoring date for that ledger's supply-side kill switch: the Sep flash showed services HICP 3.2% (from 3.0%) and core 2.5% (from 2.4%) with headline 3.8% and energy 18.8%, so the complete release confirms or revises whether the shock is spreading from energy into services, the last full inflation datum the ECB Council sees before 10-29. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately: no house playbook is rates-keyed and no tracked name carries euro-inflation exposure; the same coverage-gap reasoning as eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17. Initial research 2026-10-13 (docs/research/events/eurostat-hicp-final-2026-10-16.md) writes this canonical file over the single proposal eurostat-hicp-final-2026-10-16.from-ecb-decision-2026-10-29.json, which is now shadowed. Date, status and impact UNCHANGED (estimate, low). The substantive finding: the Sep flash already put services at 3.2%, above the 3.0% line the ECB ledger's supply-side kill names, so this release adjudicates a kill rather than revealing a number. Estimates widen caution and license nothing.
